fkr: Realistic Fake Data Generator for the Philippines

Source: R/faker-package.R
fkr-package.Rd

fkr generates realistic, locale-aware synthetic data for the Philippines: personal data (names, sex, civil status, ages, birthdays, contact details, addresses, government-ID-style numbers) and business data (company names, industries, job titles, departments, products, prices, and permit numbers).

Conventions

  • Every generator's first argument is n, the number of values to draw.

  • Generators sample with replacement, so duplicate values are possible and expected, just as they would be in a real population sample.

  • Use fkr_seed() before a sequence of calls to make them reproducible.

  • Restriction arguments (e.g. sex, region) are validated against a fixed, documented set of categories and raise an informative error (listing the valid choices) when given anything else.

  • Multi-field results (e.g. fkr_address()) are returned as a data.frame with one row per generated record, never as nested lists, so results compose directly with cbind() / dplyr::bind_cols().

Important disclaimer

Every value produced by this package – including values formatted to resemble government identifiers (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, TIN, PhilSys) – is drawn uniformly at random purely for software testing, prototyping, and teaching. These values are synthetic: they are not derived from, do not belong to, and will not validate against any real individual, business, or government record.
